Which sequence of sentences P, Q, R and S makes the most logical paragraph?
P. Attendance among senior citizens has since risen every month.
Q. With the free glasses, these readers could again enjoy newspapers and books in the reading room.
R. Many older readers had stopped coming because they could no longer see small print.
S. The city library began lending reading glasses to visitors last year.

reveal.terms: Paragraph order: the topic sentence needs nothing before it; pointer words (this, these, such, they) and transitions (however, therefore, as a result) must follow what they refer to.
reveal.shortcut: Find the sentence that can stand first on its own, then chain each pointer word to the sentence it points back to.
reveal.why_correct: Answer: "S-R-Q-P". The first sentence names the program, the second explains the problem it answers, "these readers" in the third points back to the older readers, and the fourth gives the result. Read in this order, every pointer word has something before it to refer to.

why_wrong.o2: This opens with a supporting sentence; the topic sentence must come first.

The survey covered sari-sari stores, small hardware stores and food stalls near public schools. Shoppers had to ask, and some said they received different prices on different days. Under consumer protection rules, goods offered for sale should carry a clear price tag. The city's trade office began a campaign that combined reminders and inspections. Inspectors first visited stores to explain the rule and gave out free price tag sheets. A month later, they returned to check.
